lessons.title: m, t, a
lessons.detail: The first three letters are introduced together so reading can begin immediately.

lessons.title: n
examples: nap, pin, tin, man, an, in

lessons.title: o
examples: on, top, pot, dot, mom, not

lessons.title: Ending in S
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases
lessons.detail: Final s can spell /s/ or /z/ and can mark more than one.

lessons.title: e
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases
examples: bed, pet, ten, net, men, get

lessons.title: h
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases
examples: hat, hit, hop, hen, ham, had, him, his, has

lessons.title: Heart Words
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases
lessons.detail: Introduces high-frequency words with spellings not yet taught.

lessons.title: l
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases

lessons.title: c
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases

lessons.title: u
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases
lessons.detail: Completes the five short-vowel letters.

lessons.title: r
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases
lessons.detail: for and are appear constantly in real books, so they are learned early by heart; their spellings are explained with Bossy R in Module 8.

lessons.title: z
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases

lessons.title: Module 2 Review
lessons.module_title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases

lessons.title: sh
lessons.detail: sh spells one sound.

lessons.title: ch, tch
lessons.detail: One sound, two spellings. tch commonly follows a short vowel.
examples: chip, chat, chin, much; catch, match, itch

lessons.title: y
lessons.detail: Introduces y as a consonant.

lessons.title: k, ck
lessons.detail: One /k/ sound, two spellings. ck commonly follows a short vowel and never means two /k/s.
examples: kid, kit, Ken, skip; back, sock, click, neck

lessons.title: qu
lessons.detail: q is paired with u.

lessons.title: f
lessons.detail: f spells /f/.
examples: fan, fit, fun, fog, fast, if, fish, fetch

lessons.title: ff, ll, ss, zz
lessons.detail: Doubled letters make one sound.
examples: off, bell, miss, buzz, hill, less, mess

lessons.title: th — both sounds
lessons.detail: th has voiced and unvoiced sounds.

lessons.title: w, wh
lessons.detail: Introduces w and wh.
examples: wet, win, wag, will, well, with; when, whip, which

lessons.title: ng and nk
lessons.detail: ng and nk are read as glued chunks. Only true short-vowel chunks appear here: a and i shift before ng and nk, so -ing comes next lesson and ink/ank come early in Module 5.
examples: honk, bonk, chunk, sunk, dunk, trunk

lessons.title: -ing
lessons.detail: The glued -ing chunk: first in one-beat words, then as an ending that adds a beat. Only clean base + ing words here — no doubling (running) or drop-e (making) bases; those wait for Lesson 54.

lessons.title: Meet the Vowels
lessons.detail: Vowels can spell short sounds or their names.
examples: he, she, we, me, be, hi, no, so, go

lessons.title: Magic E → i_e
lessons.detail: The final e is silent and makes the preceding vowel long.
examples: bit→bite, hid→hide, kit→kite, slid→slide, rip→ripe, spin→spine

lessons.title: j + dge
lessons.detail: j and dge spell /j/; dge commonly follows a short vowel.
examples: jam, jet, jog, jab, just, jump; badge, bridge, fudge, edge

lessons.title: a_e
lessons.detail: a_e spells /ā/.
examples: cape, made, late, make, take, came

lessons.title: v
lessons.detail: v spells /v/.

lessons.title: o_e
lessons.detail: o_e spells /ō/.

lessons.title: x
lessons.detail: Completes all 26 letters.

lessons.title: u_e
lessons.detail: u_e spells long u.

lessons.title: e_e
lessons.detail: e_e is a rare spelling of /ē/.

lessons.title: -old and -ost
lessons.detail: In these small word families, o spells /ō/ before two consonants. Treat them as families, not a general rule.

lessons.title: -ind and -ild
lessons.detail: In these small word families, i spells /ī/ before two consonants. Treat them as families, not a general rule.

lessons.title: Lowercase letters
lessons.detail: Consolidates lowercase forms, especially letters whose shapes differ from their capitals.
examples: c/C, o/O, s/S, v, w, x, z, k, p, t, u…

lessons.title: ink and ing
lessons.detail: i shifts its sound before nk and ng, so ink and ing are read as glued chunks. ing returns from Lesson 31, now in lowercase.
examples: think, pink, sink, drink, wink, stink

lessons.title: ank and ang
lessons.detail: a shifts its sound before nk and ng, so ank and ang are read as glued chunks.
examples: thank, bank, sank, tank, drank, blank

lessons.title: Soft c
lessons.detail: c followed by e commonly spells /s/.
examples: face, race, ice, mice, nice, space

lessons.title: Soft g
lessons.detail: g followed by e commonly spells /j/.

lessons.title: Reading Two-Syllable Words
lessons.detail: Extends two-syllable reading beyond -ing words, in three rungs: two known words, then a known chunk + a known word (un- means not; re- means again), then true splits.

lessons.title: -es endings
lessons.detail: After s, x, sh, ch, or tch, plural -es spells /iz/ and adds a syllable.
examples: dishes, boxes, foxes, catches, wishes, buses

lessons.title: Consonant-le
lessons.detail: Final consonant-le forms a common unstressed syllable.

lessons.title: -ed endings
lessons.detail: -ed marks past tense and can spell /t/, /d/, or /id/.

lessons.title: Endings that change the base
lessons.detail: Before -ing or -ed, a base can double its last consonant or drop its Magic E. A doubled consonant keeps the vowel short; a single consonant hints the vowel is long. Completes the -ing story from Lesson 31.

lessons.title: Open chunks
lessons.detail: Open syllables use long vowels; unstressed vowels may reduce to /uh/.

lessons.title: Vowel Y
lessons.detail: Final y commonly spells /ī/ in short words and /ē/ in longer words.
examples: my, try, why, fly, by, sky
happy, funny, silly, baby, only, quickly

lessons.title: Module 5 Review
lessons.detail: Review plus the first timed fluency check.

lessons.title: Vowel Teams → ee
lessons.detail: Two vowels can work together to spell one sound.
examples: see, tree, three, feet, keep, sleep

lessons.title: ea
lessons.detail: ea commonly spells /ē/ and sometimes /ĕ/.

lessons.title: ai
lessons.detail: The /ā/ vowel team used inside words. Revisit said, learned by heart in Module 3.

lessons.title: ay
lessons.detail: ay commonly spells /ā/ at word ends.

lessons.title: oa
lessons.detail: oa spells /ō/.

lessons.title: oo — both sounds
lessons.detail: oo has two common sounds.
examples: moon, food, zoo, too, soon, room

lessons.title: aw
lessons.detail: The /aw/ sound at the ends and inside words.

lessons.title: au
lessons.detail: A second spelling of /aw/, usually inside words.

lessons.title: all and al
lessons.detail: all is a dependable chunk. al can spell the sound in always or the sound in calm; in walk and talk, l is silent.

lessons.title: Just-Read Day I
lessons.detail: Fluency practice; no new spelling.

lessons.title: ie — both sounds
lessons.detail: ie commonly spells /ī/ at word ends and /ē/ inside words.

lessons.title: igh
lessons.detail: igh spells /ī/.

lessons.title: ou — four sounds
lessons.detail: ou can spell the vowel sounds in out, soup, young, or could.

lessons.title: ow — both sounds
lessons.detail: ow spells the sound in cow or the /ō/ sound in snow.

lessons.title: oi
lessons.detail: The /oy/ sound inside words.

lessons.title: oy
lessons.detail: The same sound at word-ends.

lessons.title: ew
lessons.detail: ew commonly spells long u or /oo/.

lessons.title: ue
lessons.detail: ue commonly spells long u or /oo/ at word ends.

lessons.title: Contractions
lessons.detail: An apostrophe marks omitted letters.
examples: it's, I'm, don't, that's, didn't, I'll, you're, let's, can't, he's, there's, wasn't, you'll, couldn't, I've, what's, they're, we're, won't, doesn't, she's, we'll, isn't, I'd

lessons.title: Just-Read Day II
lessons.detail: Fluency practice; no new spelling.

lessons.title: Bossy R → ar
lessons.detail: r changes the sound of the vowel before it; ar spells /ar/. Revisit are, learned by heart in Module 2.

lessons.title: or
lessons.detail: or spells /or/. Revisit for, learned by heart in Module 2 and now fully decodable.
examples: or, fork, corn, storm, sport, for

lessons.title: er
lessons.detail: er commonly spells /er/, especially in final syllables.
examples: her, fern, over, never, water, very

lessons.title: ir
lessons.detail: A second spelling of the /er/ sound.

lessons.title: ur
lessons.detail: er, ir, and ur spell the same /er/ sound.

lessons.title: ar and or can say /er/
lessons.detail: In an unstressed final syllable, ar or or can spell /er/.
examples: dollar, collar, polar, solar; doctor, actor, motor, author

lessons.title: are
lessons.detail: are spells the r-controlled sound in care.

lessons.title: air
lessons.detail: air spells the same r-controlled sound as are.

lessons.title: ear — four sounds
lessons.detail: ear can spell the r-controlled sounds in bear, hear, heard, or heart.

lessons.title: ore
lessons.detail: A second spelling of the /or/ sound.

lessons.title: -er & -est
lessons.detail: -er compares two; -est compares three or more.

lessons.title: Just-Read Day III
lessons.detail: Fluency practice; no new spelling.

lessons.title: eigh
lessons.detail: A rare but real spelling of /ā/.

lessons.title: ph
lessons.detail: A rare second spelling of /f/, mostly in Greek-origin words.

lessons.title: aught
lessons.detail: A dependable /awt/ chunk in a small word family.

lessons.title: ough
lessons.detail: A focused set of high-frequency words in which ough has several pronunciations.

lessons.title: oe
lessons.detail: oe can spell /ō/; in heroes, poem, and poet, o and e cross an ending or syllable boundary.

lessons.title: ey — both sounds
lessons.detail: ey can spell /ē/ as in key or /ā/ as in they. Their is introduced here as a related heart word after they is secure, not as an ey example.

lessons.title: Just-Read Day IV
lessons.detail: Fluency and expression practice; no new spelling.

lessons.title: kn
lessons.detail: The k is silent.

lessons.title: wr
lessons.detail: The w is silent.

lessons.title: mb
lessons.detail: The final b is silent.

lessons.title: Three-syllable words
lessons.detail: Extends syllable reading to three-syllable words.
examples: banana, elephant, wonderful, finally, suddenly, yesterday, grandmother, butterfly, every

lessons.title: Choose your own book
lessons.detail: Independent-book selection and reading practice.

lessons.title: Cumulative Review
lessons.detail: Cumulative review and Fluency Check IV.

lessons.title: Graduation 🎓
lessons.detail: Independent final reading and graduation.

rules.title: The target
rules.text: Fluent on grade-1 text: ~60 words correct per minute at 95%+ accuracy.

rules.title: Uppercase first
rules.text: All reading is intentionally uppercase through Lesson 44. Lowercase forms are consolidated in Lesson 45 before lowercase running text begins.

rules.title: Teach reading from print to sound
rules.text: Readers meet the letters on the page first and decode them into sounds. Organize lessons around one spelling pattern and the sound or sounds it can represent—not around one sound followed by a list of all its possible spellings. Introduce alternative spellings in separate lessons so the reader learns one new visual pattern at a time.

modules.title: First Letters, First Words
modules.theme: Introduces the first nine letters and builds the first decodable words.

modules.title: Four-Letter Words & the First Special Cases
modules.theme: Adds four-letter words, final s, the first heart words, and seven more consonants.

modules.title: Letter Friends & Five-Letter Words
modules.theme: Introduces consonant digraphs, alternate consonant spellings, five-letter words, glued ng/nk chunks, oral syllable counting, and the -ing ending.

modules.title: Long Vowels & Magic E
modules.theme: Introduces long vowels and the five Magic E spellings while completing the alphabet.

modules.title: Lowercase & Big-Kid Words
modules.theme: Moves into lowercase text, the ink/ing and ank/ang chunks, soft c and g, two-syllable words, common endings, open syllables, and vowel y.

modules.title: Vowel Teams
modules.theme: Introduces common vowel teams and the aw sound family.

modules.title: More Vowel Teams & Sound Adventures
modules.theme: Adds reading mileage, more vowel teams, flexible vowel spellings, and contractions.

modules.title: Reading Mileage & Bossy R
modules.theme: Introduces Bossy R, its core spellings, unstressed endings, and common r-controlled variants.

modules.title: Fluency & Alternate Spellings
modules.theme: Builds fluency and introduces rare or alternate spellings.

modules.title: Advanced Spellings & Graduation
modules.theme: Bridges to independent reading through expression, silent letters, longer words, review, and graduation.

reference.name: Finger Words
reference.how: Give each sound a finger, touch and say the sounds, then slide across the knuckles to blend the word.

reference.name: Letter Setter
reference.how: Say a word aloud. The reader gives a thumbs-up if it contains the target sound and a thumbs-down if it does not.

reference.name: Teach Tam
reference.how: At the end of the lesson, the reader teaches Tam the new idea in their own words. Explaining it provides a quick understanding check.

reference.name: Sticky Sounds
reference.how: Identify sounds that connect smoothly to the sound after them and blend through the connection without adding an extra vowel.

reference.name: Imaginary Finger Words
reference.how: Perform Finger Words mentally, without using a hand, as a bridge toward automatic decoding.

reference.name: Buzz Check / Buzzer
reference.how: Notice whether the voice box buzzes to distinguish voiced and unvoiced sounds, including the two sounds of s and th.

reference.name: Flexible Sounds
reference.how: Try the spelling's first common sound; if it does not form a real word, switch to the other taught sound.

reference.name: Heart Words
reference.how: Map the sounds the reader already knows, identify the unexpected spelling, and learn only that part by heart.

reference.name: Story Words
reference.how: Find a newly learned heart word inside real sentences, then read each complete sentence.

reference.name: Brain Words
reference.how: Quickly reread previously decoded words so they become instantly recognizable and free attention for meaning.

reference.name: Narrative Ninja
reference.how: Reread a sentence carefully, hear an adult model it, then read it smoothly with expression.

reference.name: Word Chains
reference.how: Read a sequence in which one letter changes at a time, such as ran → ram → ramp → camp.

reference.name: Letter Friends
reference.how: Treat two letters that spell one sound as a single unit, such as sh or ch. Find the pair before blending the word.

reference.name: Meet Syllables
reference.how: Listen to spoken words and clap or count their beats, then connect the -ing beat to the ends of written words.

reference.name: Meet the Vowels
reference.how: Identify the five vowel letters and discover that each can spell a short sound or its letter name.

reference.name: Magic E
reference.how: A silent final e changes the preceding vowel from its short sound to its long sound.

reference.name: Lowercase Telling-Apart
reference.how: Match capitals with lowercase partners, then spend extra time comparing shape-shifters and confusable forms such as b and d.

reference.name: Two-Syllable Splitting
reference.how: Begin with compounds, then prefixed words, then find the vowels, split between consonants, read each chunk, and join the chunks.

reference.name: Open Chunks
reference.how: When a syllable ends in a vowel, try the vowel's long sound before joining the chunks.

reference.name: Lazy Vowel
reference.how: In an unstressed syllable, try the relaxed /uh/ sound when the carefully decoded word sounds almost right.

reference.name: Fluency Checks I–IV
reference.how: Use an unpracticed timed passage to measure accurate words per minute and chart growth. The final check uses two grade-1 passages and keeps the stronger score.

reference.name: Vowel Teams
reference.how: Treat two neighboring vowel letters that spell one sound as a single unit.

reference.name: Just-Read Days
reference.how: Add no new spelling. Read a longer connected text for accuracy, smoothness, stamina, and enjoyment.

reference.name: Repeated Reading
reference.how: Read the same passage again, moving from accurate decoding toward smooth, expressive reading.

reference.name: Bossy R
reference.how: Notice that r changes the vowel sound before it, then connect ar, or, er, ir, ur, and later r-controlled spellings.

reference.name: Reading with Expression
reference.how: Use punctuation as a performance guide: questions rise, exclamations carry energy, and quotation marks signal dialogue.

reference.name: Five-Finger Rule
reference.how: Read one page of a possible independent book and raise one finger for each stuck word. Five fingers means save the book for later.

reference.name: Cumulative Review
reference.how: Revisit the major patterns, heart words, books, and games from all ten modules before the final fluency check.

reference.name: Graduation
reference.how: The reader completes a final book independently, celebrates the milestone, and receives guidance for continued daily reading.

contractions.rule_strong: Before Lesson {n}, make sure every contraction's full phrase has already been practiced in earlier lesson sentences or books.
contractions.rule_text: The reader should be able to read and understand the uncontracted phrase before learning the shortened form with an apostrophe.
contractions.phrases_html: Practice cannot, it is, I am, I am not, do not, that is, did not, I will, you are, let us, he is, there is, was not, you will, could not, I have, what is, they are, we are, will not, does not, she is, we will, is not, and I would or I had before introducing their contracted forms.
